findings.F1: The book's whole profit comes from trades held longer than 30 days. Those 515 trades averaged +33.8% net, won 69.7% of the time and summed to +17,412%, against a total book P&L of +9,206%. Every shorter bucket lost on average: 241 trades of 1 day or less averaged −6.26% with a 1.2% win rate, 332 trades of 1–3 days averaged −6.54% (4.5% win rate), 526 trades of 3–10 days averaged −5.77% and 611 trades of 10–30 days averaged −2.44%. These short trades are 1,710 of the 2,228 trades, all of them long.
findings.F2: Bars just above the 200-day SMA (forecast 0–5, n=1,909) had a mean next-20-bar return of −0.25%, a median of −1.65% and a 38.8% hit rate. Flat bars (n=7,297) had +2.60% mean and 43.0% hit. The 15–20 forecast bucket had +6.30% mean but a −0.11% median and 40.0% hit, so the edge from a larger distance is in the mean only.
findings.F3: Forward 20-bar returns while long are strongly right-skewed. Long bars had skew 4.30 (mean +3.22%, median −0.53%), against skew 1.23 when flat (mean +2.60%, median +0.60%). In raw distance, the top decile (mean 108% above the SMA, 20-day vol 0.064) had a −2.40% median and a 37.5% hit rate, the lowest of all deciles.
findings.F4: Whether being above the SMA helped depended on 20-day momentum. Long bars in the bottom 20-day-momentum quintile (≤ −13.9%) returned −4.75% over the next 20 bars, against +2.74% for flat bars in the same quintile. Long bars in the top two quintiles returned +5.56% and +6.54%, against +1.61% and +3.11% for flat bars.
findings.F5: Time spent in a state matters on both sides. Bars that had been below the SMA for 60–150 days returned −1.29% over 20 bars with a 32.5% hit rate (n=1,492). Bars below for 5–60 days returned +3.95% to +4.36% with hits of 47–48%. Bars above for 60–150 days had a +6.01% mean but only a 34.3% hit rate.
findings.F6: The cross events themselves show little continuation. After an upward cross (n=278), the next 5 bars returned +0.05% and the next 20 returned +2.47% (median +1.57%, hit 44.6%). After a downward cross (n=280), the next 5 bars returned +0.92%, a short-term bounce, while the next 20 had a +1.09% mean but a −1.30% median and a 39.6% hit rate.
findings.F7: Saturday is a positive return day across the sample. Pooled Saturday daily return was +0.44% (t=5.41), with positive t in all six coins (1.40 to 2.92) and t≥2.8 in 2019, 2020, 2024 and 2025. It was not positive in 2022 (t 0.42) or 2023 (t −0.01). On long bars the book earned +0.86% on Saturdays (t 4.43) and +0.63% on Fridays (t 3.52), against −0.42% on Tuesdays (t −2.24) and −0.41% on Thursdays (t −2.12).
findings.F8: Large daily moves partly reverse the next day. After a drop of 2 standard deviations or more (n=366), the next day averaged +1.78% and the next 5 days +1.97%. After a rise of more than 2 standard deviations (n=495), the next day averaged −0.52%. After ordinary days (within ±1 sd), the next day averaged +0.05%.
findings.F9: The long-versus-flat edge disappears in high volatility. Next-20-bar return for long bars minus flat bars was +2.25 points in the low 20-day-vol tercile and +2.56 points in the middle tercile, but −0.01 points in the high tercile (3.20% vs 3.21%). Even so, the book's mean daily return on long high-vol bars was the largest of the three (+0.40% vs +0.15% in the low tercile).
findings.F10: The signal's value flips by year and by coin. Long bars underperformed flat bars over 20 bars in 2018 (−17.0% vs −6.9%), 2020 (+6.4% vs +16.0%), 2021 (+4.8% vs +12.4%) and 2022 (−9.2% vs −0.9%), and outperformed in 2019 and 2025. ZEC long bars returned +8.2% vs +2.5% flat, while XRP long bars returned +4.1% vs +7.9% flat and LTC +0.6% vs +0.9%.
findings.F11: The book's extreme days fall in stretched, high-vol conditions. The best 1% of book days (mean +26.7%) came at a mean distance of 132% above the SMA after +71% 20-day momentum. The worst 1% (mean −21.9%) came at 80% above after +27% momentum. Both had 20-day vol of about 0.073 against 0.042 on other days. The top 5% of book days account for 2.9× to 16.5× the net book sum per coin, and for XMR the net is near zero or negative (share −96.5).

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above its 200-day average and its own 20-day return is strongly negative, the coin keeps falling over the next 20 bars. It does worse than it does on bars below the average with the same weak momentum.
ideas.consequence: A trader long on the "above the average" condition should step aside when the coin's recent 20-day momentum has turned sharply down.
ideas.name: above-average weak-momentum decline

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above its 200-day average and its own 20-day return is among its strongest, the coin rises further over the next 20 bars than it does at other times.
ideas.consequence: A trader should hold a long position above the average mainly while 20-day momentum is strongly positive.
ideas.name: above-average strong-momentum continuation

ideas.idea: When a coin's close sits only slightly above its 200-day average, the next 20 bars more often end lower than the coin's usual drift. This holds most often in the weeks right after an upward cross.
ideas.consequence: A trader should not buy a coin merely because it has edged above its long average.
ideas.name: marginal-cross whipsaw drift lower

ideas.idea: When a coin's close sits very far above its 200-day average with high recent volatility, the typical next-20-bar outcome is a decline. The average is held up only by a few very large further rallies.
ideas.consequence: A trader long in such stretched conditions should expect to lose on most entries and depend on rare outsized winners, so should size the position for that.
ideas.name: stretched-above median decline

ideas.idea: When a coin has stayed below its 200-day average for a long stretch of months, it keeps falling over the next 20 bars more often than it rises.
ideas.consequence: A trader should refuse bottom-fishing longs in a coin that has spent a long time below its long average.
ideas.name: prolonged-below continued weakness

ideas.idea: When a coin has recently dropped below its 200-day average, within the past several weeks, it rises over the next 20 bars more than its usual drift. The rise starts with a short bounce in the first days after the cross down.
ideas.consequence: A trader can treat a fresh drop below the long average as a short-term buying opportunity rather than an exit signal.
ideas.name: fresh-break-below rebound

ideas.idea: After a coin closes with a daily drop that is large relative to its own recent volatility, the next day's close is higher on average.
ideas.consequence: A trader can take a one-day long after an outsized down day in a coin, or avoid selling into it.
ideas.name: large-drop next-day rebound

ideas.idea: After a coin closes with a daily rise that is large relative to its own recent volatility, the next day's close is lower on average.
ideas.consequence: A trader should avoid buying the day after an outsized up day in a coin.
ideas.name: large-rise next-day giveback

ideas.idea: A coin's Saturday close-to-close return is positive on average, and this holds for every coin in the sample.
ideas.consequence: A trader can favour holding a coin over Saturday and time entries before it.
ideas.name: Saturday positive drift

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above its 200-day average while its 20-day volatility is in its low or middle range, it rises more over the next 20 bars than when it is below the average at the same volatility.
ideas.consequence: A trader should rely on the above-average condition only when the coin's recent volatility is not elevated.
ideas.name: calm-regime above-average edge
